The Jam for Passionate Adventure Game Developers!
The purpose of the $110 Adventure Game Challenge is to encourage and support creators of graphical adventure games. The Jam lasts two weeks (See time above for the start in your local time zone) after which the games will be judged by a small panel of judges. The creator of the game the judges deem to be the best will be given $110 USD! 
Unlike some jams that claim to be focused on adventure games, the genre criteria in this jam is always strictly enforced to keep the focus squarely on adventure games and adventure game developers. See the rules below. 
You can join this discord server to chat during the course of the jam: https://discord.gg/fhrERYw 
This is the tenth year of this annual jam. You can see the games from last year here: https://itch.io/jam/109-adventure-game-challenge/results 
There will be a theme announced at the start of the jam that must be adhered to when making the game. 
Rules: 
The game must fall within the genre of graphical adventure game. If you're not sure what an adventure game is, the Wikipedia page may be of some help: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adventure_game. Also, be sure to check the FAQ at the bottom of this page. Innovation and inclusion of elements not traditionally associated with adventure games is permitted and even encouraged, but the game must be clearly and primarily a graphical adventure game. I will remove entries that are clearly not adventure games. I remove several for that reason every year. I really, really don't want to remove games people have spent time and effort developing so please understand what an adventure game is. 
Sorry but text adventures are not within the scope of this jam. It must be a graphical adventure game. 
The games will have to adhere to a theme which will be announced at the start of the jam. The purpose of having a theme is to ensure no one cheats by starting their game early, but also just as importantly to encourage creativity under pressure and new avenues of thought. As such, the theme is usually quite specific, not as vague or open to interpretation as many other game jam themes tend to be. Adherence to the theme will be strictly enforced. The game must be built around the theme in an obvious way. 
Creators are free to use any tools or assets they have the right to use. This includes tools and assets they have created prior to the start of the jam, tools and assets that are free for anyone to use, and tools and assets they have purchased a license to use. Proper credit must be given if required by the licenses for the tools and assets. 
You are free to use and discuss AI generation tools in this jam. This simple line has caused an odd amount of controversy in the past. Let me make it clear that as it stands now, AI is not remotely capable of making a fun adventure game. If a game is fun, it is entirely because of the human effort that went into it regardless of whether AI was used as part of the creation process. Also, I cannot see a reason to ban AI image generation that could assist game designers who are bad at art while allowing zero-coding adventure game creators like Adventure Creator that assist game designers who are bad at coding.
Creators of all skill levels are encouraged to join. The games will be primarily judged on game design, puzzle design, and writing. The flashy professional looking game with amazing graphics is by no means guaranteed to win. We're looking for fun, well-written, well-designed games here, even if they have some flaws. Of course if your game is so buggy that it's not fun to play, that's a problem. 
The game must be in English. You will not be judged on your English ability, but it must be understandable. 
The game must be playable on Windows. Other platforms are optional. 
A team can consist of any number of members.

Welcome to Continue Your Game: The Jam!
Jam 13: Let's Try To Not Be Superstitious About This One
In this jam, you'll have to take that one game you started - probably for a different jam - and FINISH IT. Or at least continue working on it for the rest of the month.
Now, this part is very important:
Itch.io has a devlog feature, letting you share your progress with us in form of development logs. In order to get a good rating in this jam, you will have to use this feature so we can see you making progress.
Unlike most games, your submission won't be rated by how good your game is - and, in fact, you don't have to submit anything playable.
You will be rated by the progress you show in your devlogs.
And when it's your turn to rate others' games, you should do the same. That said, this is a pretty light-hearted jam - there aren't even any rewards yet - so don't take things too seriously.
Happy gamedev, and I wish you all the best in completing your projects!
______________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________
General rules for participants
Once you join the jam, you will be required to setup an itch.io page for your game if you haven't already, and keep a series of regular devlog posts on it about your progress.
Once the submission period is complete, your entry will be voted based on your overall progress, devlog consistency, devlog clarity, and how much you learned about game development in the process. Rules:

Treat your fellow gamedevs and game enjoyers with kindness and respect.

Eclipse Publishing and Game Studios is putting up $500 and reading every single submission. There's no community voting here — no rating rings, no popularity contests, no advantage for whoever has the biggest Twitter following. Our team plays every entry and picks the winners.
We're a small indie publisher and studio, which means we're not looking for polish or scope. We're looking for the one mechanic that made us sit up. The idea that shouldn't work and does. The prototype that's rough as hell but obviously alive.
Submissions open: October 1, 2026 — 1:00 PM ET
 Deadline: October 5, 2026 — 1:00 PM ET
 Winners announced: October 10, 2026
96 hours. Theme drops when submissions open. Any engine, any team size, any genre.
Not in Eastern? That's 5:00 PM UTC / 6:00 PM UK / 7:00 PM Central Europe.
PRIZES
 1st — $[300]
2nd — $[150]
3rd — $[50]
Every entrant gets written feedback from an Eclipse reviewer.
HOW JUDGING WORKS
 Eclipse plays and scores every entry. Four criteria, weighted equally: use of the theme, how good it feels to actually play, originality of the core idea, and how much you accomplished in 96 hours.
Scope is not a category. A tight five-minute game beats a broken thirty-minute one every time.
Between the deadline and October 10, we're playing. Winners are announced on the jam page and across Eclipse's channels.
WHAT WINNING ACTUALLY GETS YOU
 Cash, a feature on Eclipse's channels, and a standing offer to pitch us the full version. No obligation, no strings. You keep everything.
CONTENT RULES
Ownership and rights
 You keep 100% ownership of your game. Entering grants Eclipse nothing except permission to show footage, screenshots, and your game's name in jam coverage, recap videos, and social posts. That's it.
Eclipse claims no publishing rights, no right of first refusal, and no equity. If we want to publish your game, we'll ask like anyone else.
Eligibility
 Open worldwide. Entrants under 18 need a parent or guardian to claim any prize.
Prizes paid via PayPal or bank transfer. If we can't legally send money to your country, we'll tell you before the deadline, not after you win.
Eclipse employees, contractors, and judges can't win. They can participate for fun.
Your submission must be

Playable on Windows, Mac, Linux, or in-browser. Browser builds get played faster. That's not a rule, just true.
Uploaded before 1:00 PM ET on October 5 with a working download or embed. Late uploads, broken links, and "DM me for the build" don't count.
Assets

Credit every third-party asset in your submission description or an in-game credits screen. Missing credits = disqualified.
Fonts and music get people sued more than art does. Check your licenses.

Falling Block Jam celebrates the combination of blocks and gravity in video games. Think Tetris, Puyo Puyo, Panel de Pon, Dr. Mario, and Lumines. For just over a week in September, participating developers will be making original falling block games within a limited window of time. Check out last year's entries for inspiration.
The jam will be held online, and anyone is free to join. Teams are welcome! There will be no voting or ranking. We are doing this for love of the game.
Theme
An optional theme will be announced when the jam starts to help jumpstart ideas.
Rules
1. Games must have block-like things that fall. That's the point of the jam! What constitutes a "block" is pretty broad, so they might be something like jellies, or fruit, or meat, or garbage, or little guys! But if you just make a racing game or something totally unrelated, it's not going to fit in. Push the boundaries, but don't disregard them.
2. Games must be made during the jam. Use of some pre-existing code and assets is ok, but submissions should be mostly made during the jam period. Projects that were published before the jam started will be removed.
3. Write "Made during Falling Block Jam 2026" in the description on your project page. This just helps me weed out spam.
4. Downloadable project pages must have screenshots, and preferably an animated GIF or video of gameplay. Nobody likes mysterious downloads, so a preview is helpful.
5. Refrain from using AI. Games obviously using AI art or audio will be removed. LLM generated code may fly under the radar, but I strongly encourage you to use your noggin instead.
6. Games shouldn't require extra software to run. They should be relatively self-contained, either playable in the browser or downloadable. If you want to make something printable or like instructions for some meta falling block live-action role playing experience, that's cool! But asking people to install python or something to run your game is a bit much.
7. Be careful double-dipping. If you make a game that happens to fit another jam that's running at the same time, that's cool! Some spammers try to submit games to EVERY jam going on, though. If your game is submitted to more than 2 other jams, it may be removed.
8. Be careful with multiple submissions. You might be part of a team on multiple games, but I generally don't expect to see one person making multiple submissions. If it looks like spam, it may get removed. Reach out if you have concerns.
9. Projects that are just a mysterious APK file will be removed. It's suspicious, I'm just sayin! If you don't know what this means, you don't need to worry about it.
Frequently Asked Questions
Here are some answers to questions I got last year.
Q: What's a game jam?
A: A game jam is an event where people make an entire game within a limited window of time. The dates and times for this jam are listed towards the top of the page.
Q: How do I submit a game?
A: When the jam starts, there will be a button near the top of this page to submit a game project. I encourage you to do this after the jam starts but before the last minute so you're not scrambling to figure it out before time runs out.
Q: What even are blocks? Do they have to fall?
A: It's a pretty relaxed jam. There should be something to do with blocks falling, but those blocks might be something like ice cream, or flowers, or dice, or robot parts! Be creative and push the boundaries, but if it's obviously not in the spirit of the jam, it doesn't belong here.
Q: How closely do I have to follow the theme of the jam?
A: The theme is a suggestion to inspire creativity and give us all something to share so that we can all look back and think, oh yeah, that's the year we did that thing together! But it's optional, so don't sweat it if you hate it.
Q: Can I come up with ideas before the jam starts?
A: Absolutely! The fun is in making the thing during the jam time window, but nobody wants to stop you from percolating on ideas beforehand.

WELCOME TO THE FILIPINO HORROR GAME JAM!
Are you a Filipino game developer, professional or aspiring, who loves horror? Do you want to create games that make players shiver while celebrating Filipino culture? Then this jam is for you.
This is the first-ever Filipino Horror Game Jam, a community-driven event designed to showcase creativity, talent, and passion for horror. Whether you're a beginner or experienced developer, this is your chance to bring your ideas to life and share them with others.
ABOUT THE JAM
This is a horror-focused game jam centered around Filipino developers, culture and stories.
The goal of the jam is to encourage originality and memorable horror experiences, while supporting the continued growth of the Filipino horror game development scene.
Join fellow developers in creating terrifying games inspired by Filipino stories, experiences and culture, and become part of a growing community dedicated to celebrating Filipino horror games.
THEME
REAL LIFE HORROR
Create a horror game inspired by a real-world fear, experience, profession, location, event, or social issue. The horror must be grounded in reality. 
Supernatural elements such as ghosts, demons, curses, magic, paranormal phenomena, or folklore creatures are not allowed.
JOIN OUR COMMUNITY
You can join our community on Discord
JAM GUIDE
 When should the game be primarily developed?
 Your game must be developed primarily during the jam period.
 Who is allowed to join the game jam?
 This is open for all beginners and experienced game developers.
 Are teams allowed, and if so, is there a limit to team size?
 Teams are allowed. There's no limit to it.
 What is the theme for this jam?
 The theme will be revealed on the start of the game jam on September 1st, 2026 at 12:00 AM
 What types of visual styles are allowed for submitted games?
 You can use any visual style. (2D, 3D, hybrid, etc.)
 Is there a specific game engine required?
 No. You can use any engine you like. Your game must be playable on at least one platform (Windows, browser, etc.)
 Are we allowed to update our games after submitting?
 You are allowed to update your game after submission, but only bug fixes are allowed during the voting period.
 What is required for a valid submission?
 Your game must be playable at the time of submission.
 Is the use of AI-generated content allowed?
 If your game contains AI-generated content, it must be clearly disclosed.
 Can I submit a game I started before the jam?
 Games should be mostly developed during the jam. You may reuse small parts (codes, systems, assets) but the core gameplay, content and experience must be created during the jam.
 Can I use pre-made assets?
 Yes, as long as you have permission to use them and you properly credit the creators.
 Can I submit multiple games?
 Yes, but each game must follow all jam rules, avoid burn out, quality over quantity.
 Can I submit an unfinished game?
 Yes. Bugs and incomplete features are acceptable.
 Is the use of AI-generated content allowed?
 If your game contains AI-generated content, it must be clearly disclosed.
 Can I include gore or disturbing content?
 Yes, but with limits, horror content such as gore, violence and disturbing themes is allowed. However, explicit sexual content (NSFW) and real-world hate or harassment are not allowed.
 What is not allowed in my game?
 NSFW or explicit sexual content is not allowed. Hate speech, harassment, or any offensive or trolling content targeting individuals or groups is also strictly prohibited.
 I found bugs after submission. Can I fix them?
 Yes, you may update your game, but, keep a dev or changelog and avoid major gameplay changes during the voting period.
 How does voting work?
 Participants and the public can vote after submissions are close. Each game will be rated based on: Use of Challenge, Scare Factor, Gameplay, Creativity, Story, Art Design and Sound Design. Winners are announced after the voting period.

Hi! We're so glad you're interested in joining the World Clean Up Day Game Jam 2026.
Whether you're an experienced game developer, an artist, a musician, or someone making their very first game, you're welcome here. Jam for the Planet is built around bringing creative people together to tackle environmental challenges through games, all while learning, collaborating, and having fun. 
For this jam, the theme is Evolution.
To reflect this, the charity that this jam will be supporting is Conservation International, an organization working to protect biodiversity, restore ecosystems, and support communities on the front lines of environmental change. This means that they will receive 50% of any funds donated by participants or sponsors... whilst the other half will go towards increasing this jams prize pool!
Once the jam ends, all eligible submissions will move into a one-week community voting period. During voting, the queue size will be 6, meaning participants will be shown six games at a time, and the unlock number will be 3, meaning you will need to vote on at least three other submissions before votes on your own game become available.
At the end of community voting, the top 10 submissions will advance to our judging round. Our judges will review each of these games using a detailed evaluation criteria, providing both scores and written feedback across the jam's judging criteria.
Judging will take place over the following week. One week after the judging period ends, the completed rubrics will be returned to the top 10 teams, giving finalists detailed feedback on their games in addition to the final results.
This jam has a total prize pool of 150 USD, from a mix of sources including sponsorships, company partners, and board members. The breakdown is as follows: 
1st place: $75. 
2nd place: $50.
3rd place: $25. 
We have generally been able to pay competitors on their own basis (I.e. if a winner requests pay-pal, we can pay them via that service), but this is subject to change if a method is deemed to be untrustworthy or has associated risk (at our discretion). However, in that unlikely event, we will do our best to find an alternative method that works for both parties. 
To contribute to the overall prize pool for this jam, please call/text us at 202-914-6474, or message an admin on our discord server. 
Want to know more about Jam for the Planet and our mission? Visit our website to learn about who we are, how we donate to charity, and the impact of our game jams. Some information on the website is pending to change. 
Have questions or want to meet the team? Join our discord where you can connect with organizers, chat with fellow developers, and stay updated on all things related to the jam! This is the best place to get your information and ask questions, as our response time is generally faster. 
Our game jam is not just about making games—it's about making a difference. Half of every dollar raised through sponsorships is donated directly to a nonprofit aligned with the jam's theme, supporting real-world environmental initiatives, whether it's reforestation, ocean cleanup, wildlife conservation, or another important cause. 
To donate, please contact us at either jamfortheplanet@gmail.com, call/text our business number (202-914-6474), or message an admin on our discord server.

HERE'S A BIG OL LIST OF HELPFUL RESOURCES, ART, AND SO ON TO MAKE YOUR GAME WITH!!!
Bungie's Marathon is unique in that it's world, aesthetics, and game mechanics grip different people for different reasons. Many love the aesthetics but can't get behind the gameplay. Many love the shooting and heat, but bounce off of its looks. The lore is hidden under miles of codices that even the most seasoned detective might have a hard time digging through, while others would play an entire game that's *just* the codex.
WELL, this is a game jam for all of us. There is a lot to take from Marathon. A lot to learn. A lot to be inspired by. This jam is about honing in on those things and being as blatant as possible. I've found that only through the most obvious version of an idea can you then strip it back to find what it is about it that belongs solely to you. So we're going to file the serial numbers off of Bungie's latest work and steal from it with our whole chests.
This is the place for:
3D printed OSR clones
hacks, rip-off, spin-offs
mechanical exploration
napkin notes for a game
aesthetic exploration
lyrical attempts
lore dives and world building
shitty 4e rip-offs
Basically, anything and everything that comes from your love/disdain of Marathon.
This jam runs for the entire month of September. So plan, write, and design your game NOW. TODAY. Nothing needs to be "finished" or "polished." You can join the discord and talk about that stuff and even playtest your vision. But mostly, this is your opportunity to JUST MAKE SOMETHING.

Theme of this Jam: Virtual Pet.
There will be at least 3 optional themes available, which you can choose for an additional challenge if you wish. The themes with the most votes, excluding the winner, will be selected as the optional ones.
Optional themes: "Life Simulation", "Monochrome" and "Expedition".
Feel free to interpret the themes as you wish and make sure to have a great time.
Timing:
The game submission period will last for 9 days (any longer, and it wouldn't be a MiniJam XD). On the other hand, the voting period for the games will last for an exact week, following the closure of the submission period.
What you MUST:
You must be 18 or older to participate.
Your game must contain erotic content (implicit or explicit).
Ensure it's marked as NSFW if it's necessary (in the metadata tab; check the "has sensitive content" checkbox).
The game must be created during the submission period of the game jam. You can modify it during the voting period, and if you haven't had enough time, you can still submit the game later.
What you CAN:
You can submit games of every genre and kink, as long as the game aligns with itch.io guidelines and includes content warnings in the game.
You can work solo or in teams.
You can use characters from your favorite IPs (Fan Games are allowed).
You can submit game assets created by you during the game jam.
What you CAN NOT:
DON'T submit games with topics like gore, pedophilia, or discrimination of any group of people (you will be banned).
Advice:
Try to be original! I know it's easy to say, but you all know how people are exhausted with visual novels and similar games. Use these Game Jams to be creative and find other ways to keep people intrigued!
Voting:
Participants in the Jam can vote for other participants' games. There are no prizes for getting a higher score, but you can learn a lot from this experience and also potentially meet people to work with. The ranked categories are:
Horniness: Does the game make you feel horny? Does it fulfill your lewd desires?
Gameplay: Is the gameplay enjoyable, or is it just a backdrop with no substance?
Uniqueness: Is it an original idea? Does it explore new concepts or try something different?
Theme: Does it adhere to the announced theme?
Presentation: Is all about how cool and engaging your game looks and sounds – the art, music, sounds, and overall vibe that makes it stand out!

Are pre created and/or purchased assets allowed?: Absolutely! If you have assets that make your work easier and you want to use them, feel free to do so.
Is using AI to generate things like general environment textures or for inspiration allowed?: Yes, there is no problem at all, although the content created by AI must be specified upon delivery.
Is it allowed to start concepting and doing basic structure work before the start date. I.E. creating project files, rough concepts for story, programming for general actions such as interactions and movement?: If you want to reuse code from previous projects and other elements, it's fine, but keep in mind that the essence of the Game Jam is to do everything (or most of it) during the game jam.
Is furry content allowed?: Yes, no problem with that.
I hope you enjoy this Game Jam. I will try to organize it every month, so stay tuned!

It's that time of year again! It's olcCodeJam Time! It doesn't matter what your level of experience is, the CodeJam welcomes all to have a go at a project with a theme and a deadline. This is a CodeJam - which means you don't have to submit only games, but applications, demonstrations and other projects are welcome, as long as they adhere to the theme. The olcCodeJams usually get a wide viewing audience, so it's a great opportunity to take some pride in your work and show your stuff!
WHEN? - Starts 25 September 2026 @ 8pm BST
Why not join our discord server and chat about code with thousands of others: https://discord.com/invite/WhwHUMV
WHAT?
The theme will be announced when the jam starts. Wait for it here, or very likely there will be a theme reveal livestream, link to be posted soon.
HOW?
Its easy! 
Register with itch.io and join the CodeJam. This will allow you to keep up to date with CodeJam activity. 
Wait for the CodeJam to begin, and the theme to be announced.
Start Programming!
Submit your entry before the deadline. Once this passes, your entry is locked and is ready to be judged!
During judging, try as many other entries as you can, stream them, post the ones you like - remember the aim is to encourage people to have fun, and receiving a rating is a great feeling!
Once the judgment period ends, the winner will be announced!
RULES!
Keep it clean, safe for work and reasonably family friendly.
If you use assets you have not created, please credit them appropriately and in accordance with their license.
Your entry should be original for this Jam.
Unlike javidx9's YouTube channel, entries can be in any programming language or framework, so you are NOT limited to using olc::PixelGameEngine (though you can, and it compiles for browser now, just saying :P ), so feel free to create your entry however you want. HOWEVER: Past CodeJams have shown that browser based entries on average get more ratings because they are easy to access. This is NOT compulsory.
The winner is decided by points awarded by the public and the community.
A judges choice award is available. It's worth 893 internet points! Minor performance improvements!
Unless otherwise announced, all dates and times, especially the deadline, is final.
Special 2026 Rule!
If you are feeling especially brave or foolish, you may want to take the Beta version of olc::PixelGameEngine 3 for a spin. Those who accept this challenge and submit will be immortalised in the header file for the rest of humanity to bask in the glow of your contribution to this Sisyphean community effort. 
What about AI then?
A CodeJam should be about you creating code, not an algorithm using someone else's code. So you are encouraged to code your entry yourself. Seasoned CodeJam-er's can spot AI slop a mile away, and will label your submission accordingly during judging. As for assets, such as imagery or music, please declare if you have used generative AI and which models you have used.
Entries which look human made WILL score higher than those using AI. If you are in doubt, jump on our discord server and share your jam progress. The community follows with interest participants progress and its a great way to validate your efforts.

We welcome you to join the online Quantum Game Jam, an event where you will collaborate with game developers, quantum physicists, visual artists, musicians, engineers and other creatives in order to develop games that connect to quantum physics either through real machinery or simply thematically! 
Materials about both game development and quantum physics as well as the event itself are provided for anyone interested, but do not feel obligated to study them!
** No previous experience in quantum physics or game development is required, you only need the curiosity and an interest in quantum games!** 
Click the "Join Jam " to register!
New to Discord or jams? Not sure how to navigate the platforms?  README 
No team yet? We help form teams in the event after we reveal the theme for the event!
Games should be related to the theme (which is revealed in the beginning of the jam). 
HOW TO PARTICIPATE THE QUANTUM GAME JAM
First step - you need to register to the jam on this page (Click "Join jam" in the banner). The jam happens on  Discord and  is streamed through Twitch.tv. Follow both! The event starts with the opening ceremony on Friday, where we tell a bit about quantum physics and game development and then reveal the THEME of the jam. Each year we have a dedicated theme of the jam that serves as the inspiration and not as a limit. If you wish to take some other angle of quantum physics or computing in your game, feel free to pitch it during the pitching phase.

After the brainstorming session you will get a chance to pitch your game idea and we will proceed with the teams-forming-session, helping you to form or join a team, and provide additional assistance in Discord for creating dedicated channels for each team and off to jamming we go! We warmly recommend using these channels for main communication as out tutors are there to help.
Our hosts and moderators of the jam will assist you with the server roles and any additional tools your team may be needing. The teams will have time until Sunday afternoon to develop the games and present them then to the world!  All games will be published through this event page together with an accompanying gameplay video and screenshots. A more detailed schedule along with introducing partners, sponsors and guest speakers will be available early. 
NEXT STEPS!
Discord will serve as the main platform for the jam, so do join our Quantum Game community in our dedicated Discord-server: Game-Set-Quanta. 
Consider using your real name or adding it to the server specific nickname and READ THE RULES OF THE SERVER at #rules-of-the-server. Rise from the ashes
Search the forgotten dead.
Stoke dying embers & give old ideas new life.
Rules
Be inspired by something that's been abandoned.
Dust off something old and bring it to life.
An idea you never started on, a project you abandoned, a forgotten TV show, or a DOS game no-one talks about.
Make anything!
Video games, physical games, music, movies, PDFs, traditional art, digital art, whatever!
Be kind. Don't crunch. Drink water. Sleep. 
Not optional.
Creativity rises from ash!
Disclose AI and asset-pack usage in your submission. We want to see what you brought back to life and celebrate the genius of your own creation.

Early to bed, late to rise

Only spend 10 or less days on the jam!

Oct 18th 
Jam End.

Late Submission Deadline. Details on late-submission will be posted here closer to jam start.

Let's Play Stream. Hosted on our Discord! We'll play everyone's games and chat about them.
Oct 31st
Winners Announced.
Who is hosting this?
Society of Play is the host of Revival Jam. A 501(c) Non-profit organization for game-developers everywhere. We strive to create a creative & safe environment for developers to grow, share knowledge, and be inspired.
Learn more on our website or join us on Discord! You do not need to be a member of our community to participate.
Common questions
What should I revive?
It can be a personal project left collecting dust, or any bygone thing forgotten to time: old VHS and laserdisk releases, home movies, forgotten ps1 games, etc.
The more it means to you the better. This imbues it with your power. 
If you are hungry for inspiration, look in:
Archive.org
Library of Congress
American Archive of Public Broadcasting
Vintage / thrift stores
Libraries and estate sales
The family attic
Can I start early?
We'd rather you waited, but we're warlocks, not cops.
Is this the first Revival Jam?
NO! Society of Play has hosted "spoopy" Halloween jams for as long as we can remember. But in 2021 we renamed it to "Revival Jam"! Last year's can be found here.
Who made that amazing header art?
c0hil! They're amazing, follow them!
Can I submit my entry to multiple jams? 
Yes! As long as your submission meets the rules and theme of our jam in addition to the other jams you're submitting to, go for it!

I've never done a game jam before...

 TO BE REVEALED AT START OF JAM

¡Te invito a mi fies- digo, gamejam! 
¿Te pasa, que quieres hacer un proyecto, pero si no hay cierta presión, lo abandonas? 
¿Y te pasa también, que si hay demasiada presión, lo abandonas? 
¡Pues no sufras más! 
La tranki jam está aquí para motivarnos a empezar nuevos prototipos, con un margen de tiempo limitado pero amplio, un tema abierto y limitaciones opcionales, y sin competición.
You are invited to my par- I mean, gamejam!
Do you ever find that you want to work on a project, but if there isn’t a certain amount of pressure, you end up giving up on it?
 And do you also find that if there’s too much pressure, you end up giving up on it?
 Well, don’t worry about it anymore!
 The tranki jam (chill jam) is here to motivate us to start new prototypes, with a limited yet flexible timeframe, an open theme, optional constraints, and no competition. 
Me llamo Anaïs y soy desarrolladora indie. Este enero lancé Nom Nom: Cozy Forest Café (que se originó en una gamejam) y este verano la app nübeLABS. Tras el lanzamiento de Nom Nom Café empecé a compartir mis experiencias en Youtube con la esperanza de ayudar a otros desarrolladores. 
Con esta jam quiero animar a desarrolladores a empezar nuevos prototipos y encontrar proyectos que les motiven (como me ocurrió a mí con Nom Nom); y  a los no-desarrolladores a participar en un primer proyecto. Hacer es la forma más rápida de aprender.
Probaré en mi canal de Youtube los juegos, siempre que:
- Tenga la capacidad de probarlas en mi equipo (Windows o Navegador)
- Sigan las normas establecidas abajo
- Pueda jugarlas en un marco de tiempo razonableI'm Anaïs and I'm an indie dev. Last January I launched Nom Nom: Cozy Forest Café (which originated in a gamejam) and this summer I launched the app nübeLABS. After the launch of Nom Nom Café I started sharing my experiences on Youtube in the hope of helping other developers.
With this jam I want to encourage developers to start new prototypes and find projects that inspire them (just as Nom Nom did for me); and non-developers to take part in their first project. Doing is the fastest way to learn.
I'll play the games on my YouTube channel, provided that:
 - I'm able to test them on my computer (Windows or Browser)
 - They follow the rules listed below
